newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Bank of Israel leaves key rate unchanged.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Israel leaves key rate unchanged.

text.p: The Bank of Israel said on Thursday its key interest rate would remain unchanged at 13.9 percent in May as part of a monetary policy aimed at keeping annual inflation within a target range of seven to 10 percent.
"Inflation is now at the higher end of the target, and it was decided it was preferable not to change the interest rates," a central bank official said.
Some analysts had predicted a slight reduction of 0.3 percentage point in the bank's key lending rate while others had forecast no change.

In March, the consumer price index rose by 1.0 percent, against forecasts of a 0.7 percent increase and following a sharp 1.2 percent gain in February. Inflation in the past 12 months totalled 10.4 percent.

"Developments in prices in recent months has pointed to the continued existence of forces endangering (achievement of the inflation target)," the Bank of Israel said in a statement announcing the May rate.

"On the other hand, the long-range development trend in the M1 money supply since the beginning of 1996 is within the inflation target and economic activity is growing at a pace that is still relatively slower than the economy's potential," it said.
